data.name: Jhalak
data.gender_notes: Jhalak is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jhala', meaning to flash or shimmer, Jhalak is a name that exudes radiance and beauty. It is a name for the one who moves with grace and agility, lighting up the world around them with their charm and charisma. The name Jhalak carries the meaning “Flash, Shimmer, Motion” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi. Parents who choose Jhalak usually hope their child will grow to embody flash, shimmer, motion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Representing the divine dance of life and the cosmos, Jhalak is a name that embodies the spirit of motion and transformation. It is a reminder to embrace change and live life to the fullest, with joy and enthusiasm.
data.etymology: Jhalak belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Flash, Shimmer, Motion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jhalak total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jhalak carries an air of elegance and charm that is deeply rooted in Hindu culture. With its association with theQueen of dance 'Jhalak Dandia', this name connotes joy, celebration, and a lively spirit. It's a name that reminds us of the vibrant and rich traditions of Indian dance and music, bringing a sense of pride and joy to those who carry it.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, Jhalak symbolizes the inner radiance and beauty that lies within each one of us. It is a reminder of the divine light that resides in every soul, urging us to shimmer and shine with grace and agility, both in our external actions and internal thoughts. It's a name that encourages us to move with the rhythm of life,, gracefully embracing the ebbs and flows of the universe and illuminating the path for others to follow.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jhalak: A fleeting glimpse, a momentary revelation of the Divine in the mundane world. A reminder of the transient nature of life and the importance of cherishing each moment.

historical_references.reference: Jhalak was a renowned courtesan who flourished during the Mughal period in India (1526-1857). She was renowned for her beauty and her ability to captivate the hearts of many, including the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.

Another reference to Jhalak is found in the epic poem 'Padmavat' by Malik Muhammad Jayasi. In this work, Jhalak is described as a maiden of exceptional beauty who, disguised as a male, entered the royal court of King Ratansen to test his virtue.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Jhalak' in modern context is often associated with Indian fashion, Bollywood movies, and digital media. On Instagram, 'Jhalak' is used as a hashtag for showcasing vibrant Indian fashion outfits. On Netflix and Amazon Prime, 'Jhalak' is the name of a popular dance reality show which gained immense popularity among audiences. These trends reflect the growing interest and influence of Indian culture globally.
